transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining me to discuss the eighth-grade civics oral-history project before I make my approval decision. I've reviewed the draft plan, and I'd like to walk through some key points together — particularly around the number of student interviewers, the use of personal phones for audio recording, publishing all recordings on the public school website, and the indefinite retention of those files. I want to make sure we've thought through the implications of each element carefully. Could I start by hearing from the project advisor about the educational goals and how this plan was developed?

transcript.text: My family-consent review has identified a critical issue: five interviewees — I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 — have not granted permission for public web publication of their recordings. Their recordings may be used only in the school's internal archive, and the plan must include a consent-exclusion record documenting this restriction. This means the draft plan's call to publish all recordings on the public school website cannot proceed as written for these five interviewees.

Second, the consent-exclusion record I flagged should be integrated into the same approval documentation as Ms. Patel's training-verification record and Ms. Romero's secure-storage configuration record, so that Dr. Morgan has a complete picture of all three compliance requirements before signing off. I'd also note that since Ms. Romero's technology review limits recordings to district tablets stored in the restricted OralHistory drive with a 45-day deletion timeline, the internal archive storage for the five restricted interviewees should fall within that same secure-storage framework. I don't have any additional findings beyond what I've already shared, but I'm happy to discuss any adjustments needed to reconcile these three sets of requirements.
